ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The attached circuit diagram shows an NPN BJT symbol. The left terminal, the base, is labeled +2 V. The upper terminal, the collector, is labeled +7 V. The lower terminal, the emitter, is labeled +1.3 V. Reasoning: For this NPN transistor, V_BE = V_B - V_E = 2.0 V - 1.3 V = 0.7 V, so the base-emitter junction is forward biased. Also, the collector is at +7 V while the base is at +2 V, so the collector-base junction is reverse biased. A BJT with forward-biased base-emitter junction and reverse-biased collector-base junction operates in the active region.
